figs.title: Secular equation for the exact trust region step
figs.caption: The exact step p(λ) = −(B + λI)⁻¹g shrinks steadily as λ grows. A radius below the Newton length sets λ* > 0 where ‖p(λ)‖ = Δ, and a radius above it gives λ = 0 and the full Newton step.

figs.title: Log variables make cruise drag convex
figs.caption: In (V, S) the drag contours bend and the Hessian is indefinite wherever parasite drag P exceeds induced drag Q (shaded). In (ln V, ln S) the same drag depends on 2 ln V + ln S alone, its contours are parallel lines, and it is convex as a geometric program.

figs.title: Metropolis acceptance in simulated annealing
figs.caption: Simulated annealing accepts every downhill move and accepts an uphill move with probability exp(−Δf/T). A hot temperature accepts most uphill moves for exploration, and cooling turns the search into local refinement.

figs.title: Minimum norm weights for an underdetermined fit
figs.caption: With fewer samples than weights, every point on the line Φw = y fits the data exactly. The minimum norm solution w = Φᵀ(ΦΦᵀ)⁻¹y is the point of that line closest to the origin, and ridge solutions approach it along Φᵀ as λ shrinks to zero.

figs.title: Reduced space versus full space formulation
figs.caption: A reduced space method converges R(x, u) = 0 inside every analysis, so the optimizer sees x alone. A full space method adds the states u to the variables and poses R(x, u) = 0 and the lift requirement as equality constraints that are met together at the optimum.
